subject: astronomy
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: The seasons on Earth are caused by:
options: The changing distance between Earth and the Sun
The tilt of the Earth's axis (about 23.5 degrees)
The Earth speeding up and slowing down
questions.explain: The 23.5 degree axial tilt changes the angle and duration of sunlight through the year, causing seasons.

questions.q: A total lunar eclipse can only happen at:
questions.explain: A lunar eclipse needs the Moon opposite the Sun in Earth's shadow, which only occurs at full Moon.

questions.q: Why is there not a solar and lunar eclipse every month?
options: The Moon's orbit is tilted about 5 degrees to the Earth's orbit, so alignment is rare
questions.explain: Because the Moon's orbit is tilted, the three bodies usually do not line up exactly each month.

questions.q: Tides on Earth are caused mainly by:
options: The gravitational pull of the Moon (and Sun)
questions.explain: The Moon's gravity, aided by the Sun, raises tidal bulges in the oceans.

questions.q: The synodic month (about 29.5 days) is longer than the sidereal month (about 27.3 days) because:
options: The Moon slows down during the month
The Earth is also moving around the Sun, so the Moon must travel further to realign with the Sun
questions.explain: The synodic month measures the cycle of phases; the extra time accounts for Earth's motion around the Sun.

questions.q: A solar eclipse can only occur at:
questions.explain: A solar eclipse needs the Moon between Earth and Sun, which only happens at new Moon.

questions.q: A sidereal day (about 23 hours 56 minutes) is slightly shorter than a solar day because:
options: The Earth spins faster at night
The Earth must rotate a little extra to face the Sun again as it orbits
questions.explain: A sidereal day is one rotation relative to the stars; the solar day needs extra rotation to re-face the Sun.

questions.q: Why is the lunar surface so heavily cratered compared with most of the Earth's surface?
options: The Moon has almost no atmosphere or weather to erode or burn up impactors
The Moon attracts more meteors than Earth
The Moon is made of softer rock
questions.explain: Without an atmosphere, water or plate tectonics, impact craters on the Moon are preserved for billions of years.

questions.q: We always see the same face of the Moon from Earth because:
options: The Earth blocks the other side
The Moon's rotation period equals its orbital period (synchronous rotation)
The far side is always dark
questions.explain: The Moon is tidally locked: it rotates once per orbit, so the same hemisphere always faces Earth.

questions.q: A lunar eclipse occurs when:
options: The Sun is hidden behind the Moon
The Moon passes between the Earth and the Sun
The Moon enters its own shadow
The Earth passes between the Sun and the Moon, casting its shadow on the Moon
questions.explain: In a lunar eclipse the Earth lies between Sun and Moon and the Moon passes into Earth's shadow.

questions.q: Why does the same hemisphere of the Moon always face away from Earth, making it the 'far side'?
options: The Moon does not rotate at all
The Moon is tidally locked, rotating once per orbit
The Earth's atmosphere blocks our view of it
questions.explain: Tidal locking means the Moon's rotation period equals its orbital period, so one hemisphere is permanently turned away from Earth.

questions.q: The Earth's revolution refers to its:
options: Orbit around the Sun, taking one year
questions.explain: Revolution is the Earth's yearly orbit around the Sun, while rotation is its daily spin.

questions.q: The dark, flat plains on the Moon are called maria. They are:
options: Large impact craters filled with ice
questions.explain: Maria are vast plains of solidified basaltic lava that look dark and smooth.

questions.q: Roughly how many days does it take the Moon to complete one full cycle of phases?
questions.explain: One complete cycle of lunar phases (the synodic month) takes about 29.5 days.

questions.q: Spring tides (the highest high tides) occur when:
options: The Sun and Moon pull at right angles
The Moon is farthest from Earth
The Sun and Moon are aligned at new and full Moon
questions.explain: At new and full Moon the Sun and Moon align, combining their gravitational pulls to give spring tides.

questions.q: In an eclipse, the region of total shadow is called the:
questions.explain: The umbra is the dark, fully shadowed central region; the penumbra is the partial outer shadow.

questions.q: In an annular solar eclipse a ring of sunlight remains visible because the Moon:
options: Is exactly the same apparent size as the Sun
Is slightly too far from Earth to cover the Sun completely
Is between the Earth and Sun at full Moon
questions.explain: When the Moon is near apogee its apparent size is too small to fully cover the Sun, leaving a bright ring (annulus).

questions.q: Neap tides (the smallest range between high and low tide) occur when:
options: The Sun and Moon are at right angles to each other (first and last quarter)
The Sun and Moon are in line
The Earth is closest to the Sun
questions.explain: At the quarter Moons the Sun and Moon pull at right angles, partly cancelling and giving neap tides.

questions.q: The phases of the Moon are caused by:
options: Different amounts of the sunlit half of the Moon being visible from Earth
The Moon producing its own light
The Earth's shadow falling on the Moon
Clouds covering part of the Moon
questions.explain: Phases occur because we see varying portions of the Moon's sunlit hemisphere as it orbits Earth.

questions.q: During a total solar eclipse, the part of the Sun's atmosphere visible around the Moon is the:
questions.explain: With the bright photosphere hidden, the faint outer corona becomes visible during totality.

questions.q: The Earth's rotation on its axis is responsible for:
questions.explain: As the Earth rotates once every 24 hours, places move into and out of sunlight, giving day and night.

questions.q: It is summer in the Northern Hemisphere when:
options: The North Pole is tilted towards the Sun
The Earth's axis is not tilted
The Earth is closest to the Sun
questions.explain: Northern summer occurs when the North Pole tilts towards the Sun, giving longer days and higher Sun.
